items.title: Cardiovascular Outcomes of Insulin Degludec Versus Insulin Glargine in Trial-Eligible and Ineligible Populations: A DEVOTE-Inspired Target Trial Emulation Using the Swedish National Diabetes Register.
items.abstract: To compare cardiovascular outcomes associated with the initiation of insulin degludec versus insulin glargine using a target trial emulation approach in nationwide real-world data. We conducted a nationwide observational cohort study using Swedish health registers, including the National Diabetes Register. Individuals with type 2 diabetes initiating insulin degludec or insulin glargine between 2012 and 2022 were included. Two complementary approaches were applied: a trial-eligible emulation cohort reflecting the eligibility criteria of the DEVOTE trial, and a trial-ineligible emulation cohort representing routine clinical practice. The primary outcome was major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE, i.e., myocardial infarction, stroke and cardiovascular mortality). Secondary outcomes included the individual components of MACE, all-cause mortality and heart failure. Average treatment effects were estimated using longitudinal targeted minimum loss-based estimation. Among 96 731 individuals identified, 44 890 met the study eligibility criteria and were included in the analyses. In the trial-eligible cohort, degludec was associated with a similar risk of MACE compared with glargine (risk ratio: 1.10; 95% CI: 0.91-1.34; p = 0.34), but a significantly lower risk of all-cause mortality (risk ratio: 0.75; 95% CI: 0.62-0.92; p = 0.002). In the trial-ineligible emulation cohort, degludec was associated with lower risks of MACE (risk ratio: 0.80; 95% CI: 0.67-0.95; p = 0.004) as well as reduced risks of all-cause mortality, cardiovascular mortality, non-fatal stroke and heart failure. In this nationwide study, degludec was associated with a lower risk of all-cause mortality compared with glargine, consistently observed in both trial-eligible and trial-ineligible populations, despite similar cardiovascular risk in the trial-eligible cohort.

items.title: Performance of artificial intelligence-based coronary CT angiography-derived fractional flow reserve across cohorts with different prevalence of obstructive coronary artery disease.
items.abstract: Coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) provides accurate anatomical assessment of coronary stenosis severity but has limited ability to determine lesion-specific ischemia as assessed by invasive fractional flow reserve (FFR). We aimed to evaluate the diagnostic performance of an artificial intelligence-based deep learning CCTA-derived FFR model (CT-FFR AI ) in cohorts undergoing CCTA and invasive FFR as part of a study protocol and a real-world cohort undergoing invasive FFR based on suspected coronary artery disease on CCTA in routine clinical care. Diagnostic performance of CT-FFR AI (CorEx, SPIMED-AI) was evaluated using an intention-to-diagnose approach and compared with CCTA using 50% and 70% stenosis thresholds, with invasive FFR as reference standard. In the PACIFIC-1 study cohort, 208 patients underwent CCTA and invasive FFR assessment of all major coronary vessels irrespective of CCTA findings. The real-world cohort included 202 patients with at least one CCTA-defined lesion ≥70% stenosis who underwent ICA with invasive FFR. In the PACIFIC-1 cohort (612 vessels), per-vessel diagnostic accuracy was comparable between CT-FFR AI (77%), when using a CCTA based ≥50% stenosis threshold (76%; P = 0.689), and when using a ≥70% stenosis threshold (74%; P = 0.183). In the real-world cohort (325 vessels), CT-FFR AI demonstrated higher per-vessel diagnostic accuracy (63%) compared with CCTA using ≥50% and ≥70% stenosis thresholds (52% and 57%, respectively; P AI beyond CCTA alone using ≥50% and ≥70% stenosis thresholds was 7.9% (P = 0.256) and 17.7% (P = 0.012) in the PACIFIC-1 cohort, compared with 23.2% (P < 0.001) and 13.6% (P = 0.070) in the real-world cohort, respectively. CT-FFR AI may outperform anatomic assessment alone, with diagnostic accuracy depending on the prevalence of obstructive coronary artery disease and the range of stenosis severities among vessels undergoing invasive FFR assessment.

items.title: Partial Echocardiographic Remission After Sotatercept: Expanding Treatment Goals in Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension.
Sustained improvement of systemic lupus erythematosus‑associated pulmonary arterial hypertension by CD19 CAR T-cell therapy: 1‑year haemodynamic follow‑up.
[Pulmonary rehabilitation: A 2026 updated expert consensus].
items.abstract: The effectiveness of pulmonary rehabilitation (PR) in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease is supported by a high level of evidence. More recently, the indications for PR have expanded and new models of care have emerged. This position statement summarizes recent evidence on PR regarding: 1) its objectives; 2) the key outcomes to be assessed at baseline, during, and at the end of the program, along with the recommended assessment tools; 3) its integration within the care pathway; 4) modalities of implementation, including home-based programs, telerehabilitation, and hybrid formats; 5) its core components, based on therapeutic education (including psychosocial and motivational support), exercise training, and adapted physical activity; and 6) the strategies and professionals involved in maintaining long-term benefits. The extension of PR indications to other respiratory conditions (interstitial lung diseases, pulmonary hypertension, thoracic oncology) and the development of new delivery models are expected to facilitate PR access. This position statement from French-speaking experts aims to support greater recognition of PR and to promote its integration into patient care pathways.

items.title: Impact of Organ-Specific Severe Immune-Related Adverse Events on Long-Term Survival and Treatment Transitions in Metastatic Renal Cell Carcinoma: A 5-Year Multicenter Multistate Analysis.
items.abstract: Immune-related adverse events (irAEs) frequently occur during combination immune checkpoint inhibition. However, their prognostic impact may vary according to organ involvement and severity. In this study, we exploratorily evaluated whether severe non-endocrine irAEs represent a temporally distinct and prognostically unfavorable clinical phenotype in patients with metastatic renal cell carcinoma (mRCC) treated with ipilimumab plus nivolumab. We analyzed 63 patients with mRCC treated with ipilimumab plus nivolumab who were followed for at least 5 years. Patients were categorized into non-irAE, non-severe + severe endocrine irAE, and severe non-endocrine irAE groups. Overall survival (OS) was assessed. Multistate modeling was used to evaluate the transitions between treatment, irAE occurrence, and death. Landmark analyses were performed at 8 and 12 weeks to address immortal time bias. The severe non-endocrine irAE group was associated with inferior OS. The multistate analysis revealed a potentially increased risk of direct transition from ipilimumab plus nivolumab to death in the severe non-endocrine irAE group. A significantly higher proportion of patients in the severe non-endocrine irAE group experienced irAEs within 30 days. No significant association was observed in the 8- and 12-week landmark analyses. In this exploratory retrospective study, severe non-endocrine irAEs showed an association with early onset and potentially unfavorable clinical outcomes in patients with mRCC receiving ipilimumab plus nivolumab. Given the limited sample size, these findings should be interpreted cautiously and require confirmation in larger independent cohorts.

items.title: Transcriptome Analysis Identifies a Myeloid-Like Signature in Relapsed or Refractory B-Cell Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia Patients With Poor Response to CD19 Chimeric Antigen Receptor T Cell Therapy.
items.abstract: Relapsed or refractory B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (R/R B-ALL) patients exhibit heterogeneous responses to CD19 chimeric antigen receptor T-cell (CAR-T) therapy. However, current studies primarily focus on the CAR-T cells or the leukemia blasts, and the patient's intrinsic molecular characteristics before treatment remain poorly understood. Fifteen R/R B-ALL patients enrolled in a phase II, single-arm clinical trial (NCT04684147) were stratified at a three-month landmark into 8 good responders and 7 poor responders. Clinical characteristics, genetic alterations and pre-treatment bone marrow transcriptomics were compared between groups, and an exploratory gene-expression score was derived. Differential expression and enrichment analyses identified a myeloid-like signature and upregulation of myeloid-related genes in poor responders. Seven myeloid-related genes were examined in independent patient cohorts, in B-ALL cell lines and at single-cell resolution in one patient; three were expressed by the leukemic cells themselves and four predominantly by monocytes and macrophages. A separate, variance-derived seven-gene least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) score separated response groups in the discovery cohort (apparent area under the curve, AUC 1.00), with bias-corrected and external estimates of approximately 0.57-0.59 (external cohort AUC 0.592, 95% confidence interval 0.356-0.828). Pre-treatment transcriptomic profiling revealed a myeloid-like signature in R/R B-ALL patients with poor CD19 CAR-T response, warranting further investigation as a candidate correlate of treatment outcome.

items.title: Low-Dose Nivolumab in Various Cancers: A Real-World Exploratory Analysis in Resource-Constrained Settings.
items.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs), including nivolumab, have significantly improved cancer care. However, due to high costs, there is a significant financial barrier to their widespread access. Emerging evidence shows biological plausibility as well as efficacy of low-dose nivolumab across different cancers. This exploratory study aims to investigate the clinical outcomes of low-dose nivolumab in cancer treatment to explore the potential to improve its access by reducing costs, especially in resource-limited settings. Data on patients with various malignancies treated with fixed 20 or 40 mg of nivolumab every 3 weeks were retrospectively analyzed. Response to the treatment, including the best objective response rate, best disease control rate, and adverse events, was reported. The Kaplan-Meier method was used to determine progression-free survival and overall survival. The patient cohort of 31 patients with various tumors received a median of 9 cycles (range, 2-20) of low-dose nivolumab therapy for 5.7 months (range, 0.7-17.1). Median follow-up was 8.6 months (95% CI, 7.1-12.9). Disease control was achieved in 21/31 (67.7%) patients, with the best objective response rate of 51.6%. The median progression-free survival was 8.8 months (95% CI, 6.6-not reached) and overall survival was 14.8 months (95% CI, 11.1-not reached). At the end of the study period, 3/31 patients had a radiologic complete response, 9/31 had a partial response, 4/31 had stable disease, and 6/31 had progressive disease, and 3/31 were not evaluable; 6 patients died during this period. The responses achieved were sustainable for a median of 4 months (range, 0.8-8.2). Only 5 patients developed adverse events of grade 2 or 3. Low-dose nivolumab shows preliminary efficacy in resource-constrained settings. Further research should explore optimal dosing and scheduling for low-dose immunotherapy and evaluate its efficacy and safety through larger, homogeneous studies.

items.title: MAIT cells in gastrointestinal cancer: immunity to therapy.
items.abstract: Mucosal-associated invariant T (MAIT) cells are emerging as important regulators of immunity in gastrointestinal (GI) cancers. Enriched in mucosal and hepatic tissues, MAIT cells recognize microbial-derived metabolites presented by MHC class I-related molecule (MR1) and rapidly exert effector functions, including cytokine production and cytotoxicity. Across GI malignancies, including hepatocellular carcinoma, cholangiocarcinoma, colorectal, gastric, pancreatic, and esophageal cancers, MAIT cells display context-dependent roles shaped by the tumor microenvironment, microbiome, and immune signaling pathways. While they can mediate antitumor immunity, they frequently exhibit functional exhaustion or adopt pro-tumorigenic phenotypes. Therapeutic strategies aim to enhance MAIT cell activity, reverse dysfunction, and integrate them into combinatorial immunotherapy approaches. Understanding MAIT cell biology may enable their exploitation as biomarkers and therapeutic targets in GI cancers.

items.title: Paraneoplastic Autoimmune Multiorgan Syndrome: Diagnostic Lessons for Pediatricians.
items.abstract: We report the challenging diagnosis of an 11-year-old boy, presenting with subacute erythroblastopenia, followed by a multisystemic immune-mediated syndrome characterized by polymorphic mucocutaneous manifestations, associated with severe myositis related to a dermatomyositis-like phenotype and mild hepatitis. A progressive lymphadenopathy led to a delayed diagnosis of T-lymphoblastic lymphoma associated with paraneoplastic autoimmune multiorgan syndrome. To achieve remission of this paraneoplastic syndrome, Janus kinase inhibitor was required in addition to antitumor therapy. This case highlights several key points: (1) Pediatricians should consider a paraneoplastic origin when facing juvenile dermatomyositis with atypical features, such as hematologic and mucosal abnormalities; (2) in uncertain cases, early collaboration with oncologists is needed to optimize diagnostic and therapeutic strategies; (3) the choice of immunomodulatory therapy is critical in addition to antitumor therapy.

items.title: The new landscape of liver transplantation: Evolving candidates, new technologies, and personalized care.
items.abstract: Liver transplantation (LT) is entering a new era shaped by changes in disease epidemiology, candidate complexity, donor utilization, and post-transplant management. The decline of viral hepatitis-related cirrhosis, together with the rise of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease, alcohol-related liver disease, and hepatocellular carcinoma, has transformed the LT waitlist into an older, frailer, and more cardiometabolically complex population. At the same time, donation after circulatory death and machine perfusion are expanding the donor pool and redefining the boundaries of graft suitability. Candidate selection is also moving beyond traditional diagnosis-based criteria, with increasing acceptance of early LT for carefully selected alcohol-related liver disease, utility-based transplantation for acute-on-chronic liver failure, and biology-driven transplant oncology, in which HCC is established whereas selected iCCA and unresectable CRLM indications remain investigational. In parallel, artificial intelligence and machine learning are being developed as decision-support tools for candidate assessment, waitlist prioritization, donor-recipient matching, and prediction of post-transplant outcomes; prospective validation and evidence of clinical impact remain limited. Immunosuppression is facing a similar transformation, shifting from standardized lifelong exposure toward individualized, monitored minimization and immunologic risk profiling, while complete withdrawal and operational tolerance remain restricted to highly selected recipients within specialized protocols. In this Perspective, we argue that the future of LT will depend on integrating biological reserve, disease behavior, graft quality, and expected survival benefit into transparent, multidisciplinary decision-making. The central challenge will be to translate innovation into durable clinical benefit while preserving equity in access to transplantation.

items.title: Recovery of Human Pegiviruses from Patients with Acute Febrile Illness and Sub-acute Central Nervous System Infection.
items.abstract: To describe two cases of HPgV-1 identified during high-throughput sequencing (HTS)-based investigation of previously undiagnosed acute febrile illness (AFI) and central nervous system infection. RNA metagenomic HTS was applied to clinical samples that had previously tested negative by PCR targeting alphaviruses, flaviviruses, enteroviruses, herpesviruses, and paramyxoviruses. Specimens were also tested for IgM antibodies against chikungunya virus, dengue virus, and Japanese encephalitis virus. A complete HPgV-1 genotype 4 was recovered from a child with undifferentiated AFI. In a middle-aged man with HIV and severe neurological disorder, complete genomes of HPgV-1 (genotype 4), HPgV-2, and hepatitis C virus (genotype 3k) were identified. To our knowledge, this is the first report of HPgV-2 detection in Indonesia, expanding its known geographic distribution. These findings underscore the complexity of viral co-infections in immunocompromised patients and the uncertain clinical significance of human pegiviruses. This further highlights the utility of metagenomic HTS for pathogen discovery and genomic surveillance in unexplained clinical syndromes.
items.journal: International journal of infectious diseases : IJID : official publication of the International Society for Infectious Diseases

items.title: Psychological violence, subjective well-being, and burnout among healthcare workers: The roles of sleep disturbance and perceived occupational infection risk.
items.abstract: Psychological violence (PCV), which includes verbal abuse, bullying, intimidation, sexual harassment and ethnic discrimination, is the most frequently reported form of workplace violence in health care and a well-documented correlate of burnout. Healthcare workers (HCWs) in infectious disease services face this psychosocial hazard alongside two further, structurally persistent conditions: impaired recovery through disturbed sleep, and the appraised risk of acquiring infection at work. How these demands combine with workers' personal psychological resources is not well understood. To examine (i) whether PCV exposure is associated with burnout, (ii) whether subjective well-being (SWB) functions as an intervening variable in that association, (iii) whether sleep disturbance is associated with burnout independently of SWB, and (iv) whether the strength of the SWB-burnout association depends on the level of perceived occupational infection risk. Cross-sectional survey of 675 HCWs (76.3% women) at a public tertiary infectious disease hospital in southern China (December 2022 - January 2023), a designated centre for HIV/AIDS, tuberculosis, hepatitis and, at the time of data collection, COVID-19. PCV exposure over the preceding 12 months was assessed with the ILO/ICN/WHO/PSI instrument; SWB with the WHO-5; burnout with the two-item abbreviated Maslach Burnout Inventory screen; sleep disturbance with three binary epidemiological items; and perceived occupational infection risk with a single validated item indexing appraised infection hazard in the respondent's own workplace. Conditional process analysis (ordinary least squares path analysis, 5000 bootstrap resamples) was adjusted for gender, age band, education, occupation, employment type, department and reported concern about workplace violence. PCV was reported by 34.1% of participants and sleep disturbance by 53.3%. PCV exposure was positively associated with burnout (adjusted direct association b = 0.53, 95% CI 0.11 to 0.96, P = .015; total association b = 0.72, 95% CI 0.27 to 1.19). SWB was negatively associated with burnout (b = -0.13, P < .001) and accounted for an indirect association of 0.19 (95% CI 0.05 to 0.34), approximately 26% of the total. Sleep disturbance was independently associated with burnout after adjustment for SWB and all covariates (b = 0.46 per additional sleep symptom, 95% CI 0.25 to 0.68, P < .001). Perceived occupational infection risk moderated the SWB-burnout association (interaction b = -0.038, 95% CI -0.060 to -0.016, P < .001): the association between SWB and burnout was steeper at higher perceived risk (b = -0.085 at -1 SD; -0.133 at the mean; -0.181 at +1 SD), and the conditional indirect association rose correspondingly (0.12 to 0.26; index of moderated mediation 0.054, 95% CI 0.012 to 0.112). In a workforce facing sustained occupational infection risk, PCV exposure, low SWB and disturbed sleep were each associated with greater burnout, and SWB differentiated burnout most sharply among workers appraising their workplace as most hazardous. Because the design is cross-sectional, the direction of the PCV-SWB-burnout sequence cannot be established, and reciprocal influence is likely. The findings support treating violence prevention, recovery-protective scheduling and infection-risk communication as complementary components of occupational mental health provision rather than as separate programmes.

items.title: Targeted redox gene-expression profiling reveals shared and distinct expression patterns in HBV- and HCV-associated hepatocellular carcinoma.
items.abstract: Oxidative stress and redox dysregulation are important features of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), but their expression patterns in hepatitis B virus (HBV)- and hepatitis C virus (HCV)-associated HCC remain incompletely characterized. This study investigated redox-related gene expression and its potential functional and prognostic relevance. A predefined 84-gene oxidative stress and redox-related quantitative real-time PCR array was used to profile 11 HCC samples (7 HCV-associated and 4 HBV-associated tumors) and 4 controls. Analyses included hierarchical clustering, gene-list overlap, functional enrichment, protein-protein interaction networks, gene-expression correlations, and exploratory survival analysis. Both HCC groups exhibited altered expression of genes associated with antioxidant defense, glutathione metabolism, mitochondrial redox regulation, and ferroptosis-related processes. In HCV-associated HCC versus controls, TXN, SPINK1, HSP90AA1, and DUSP1 showed increased expression. In HBV-associated HCC versus controls, GCLC, peroxiredoxins, CAT, and SOD1 showed increased expression. Eighteen genes were shared between comparison lists, including GPX4, GPX2, GPX3, PRDX1, PRDX5, TXN, GCLM, SOD2, and FTH1. Enrichment analyses implicated glutathione metabolism, oxidative stress, peroxisome function, and ferroptosis-associated processes. Network analysis identified GPX2, GPX3, GPX4, and SOD2 in a connected module. External exploratory survival analysis associated higher SPINK1 and HSP90AA1 expression with poorer overall survival. These findings identify redox-related expression patterns warranting further investigation. Larger cohorts and functional studies are needed to establish etiological differences, ferroptosis susceptibility, and prognostic significance.

items.title: Three Decades of Liver X Receptor Agonist Chemistry: Structural Motifs, Structure-activity Relationship, and Therapeutic Prospects.
items.abstract: Liver X receptors (LXRs) are nuclear receptors that play an important role in the regulation of gene expression involved in lipid metabolism, cholesterol homeostasis and inflammation. Certain modifications in endogenous LXR activity have been associated with pathological conditions and diseases. The dysregulation of LXR activity can lead to vascular and metabolic diseases, neurological degeneration and formation of malignant tumors. One of the solutions to treat the diseases or at least to slow down the progression is the development of different strategies to modulate LXR signaling for the treatment or prevention of these pathological conditions. Many researchers and pharmaceutical companies are developing selective LXR modulators to precisely control receptor activity and achieve specific pharmacological effects. The activation of LXRs has been linked to the inhibition of cell proliferation and metastasis, the promotion of apoptosis and re-differentiation of tumor cells that drives exosome release to stimulate anti-tumor immunity in certain cancer types. The main challenge is to minimize the adverse effects of LXR induction on lipid metabolism via selective activation of LXRβ isoform. Several lead compounds were identified and tested in clinical trials for few pathologies discussed above. The discovery of a potent and selective LXR ligand involves a combination of multiple steps from lead discovery, optimization, preclinical and clinical testing before getting to marketing authorization. This review offers an overview of synthetic agonists for LXRs developed over the past three decades. Though multiple investigations have been in progress, no FDA-approved LXR-targeting drug is available so far.
items.journal: The Journal of steroid biochemistry and molecular biology

items.title: Engineering exosome-based delivery of IL-37 to enhance cytokine stability and antitumor activity in vitro and in vivo.
items.abstract: Interleukin-37 (IL-37) is an anti-inflammatory cytokine with antitumor activity, yet its clinical utility is constrained by poor bioavailability and rapid degradation. This study engineered NCI-H226-derived exosomes as IL-37 nanocarriers and evaluated their anticancer efficacy in cellular and hepatic carcinoma models. Exosomes were isolated using Total Exosome Isolation (TEI) reagent and qEV10 size-exclusion chromatography. IL-37 loading by sonication achieved >80% encapsulation efficiency and sustained release, with cumulative release of 65.11 ± 0.25% and 59.95 ± 0.43% for qEV10- and TEI-isolated exosomes, respectively. IL-37-loaded exosomes exhibited greater cytotoxicity than free IL-37 across tested cancer cells. In the DEN-1 rat model, IL-37-loaded exosomes significantly reduced tumor burden, liver fibrosis, and serum ALT, AST, ALP level. Gene expression analysis showed normalization of inflammatory (IL-6, IL-1β) and fibrotic (α-Sma, Col1α1) markers. These findings support further investigation of exosome-based IL-37 delivery as a better immunotherapy platform.

items.title: Standardized Diagnosis of Lymphocytic Myocarditis at Autopsy: Application of the Seaport Criteria.
items.abstract: The histological diagnosis of lymphocytic myocarditis at autopsy is challenged by limited reproducibility and the lack of standardized criteria applicable to non-biopsy specimens. This study aimed to assess the feasibility and diagnostic performance of the new Seaport criteria for autopsy in a heterogeneous cohort of clinical autopsies. An autopsy cohort of 50 consecutive cases was retrospectively revaluated, including 10 sudden death cases originally diagnosed as lymphocytic myocarditis and 40 controls (ischemic heart disease, brain diseases, liver diseases, and metastatic neoplasms). Each case was reclassified according to Seaport criteria as myocarditis (focal, multifocal, or diffuse), lymphocytic infiltrate of uncertain significance (LIUS), or no inflammation. Immunohistochemistry (CD3, CD68, C4d) and molecular testing for viral genome were carried out in myocarditis/LIUS cases. By applying the Seaport criteria for autopsy, active lymphocytic myocarditis was confirmed in 9 of 10 originally diagnosed cases, either focal (33%) or multifocal (67%) and never diffuse; one case was reclassified as LIUS. Three additional cases among controls showed LIUS, yielding an overall LIUS prevalence of 8% in the entire series. A subepicardial confluent topography was observed in four myocarditis cases. Temporal assessment revealed subacute forms in 55.6% and acute in 44.4%. Immunohistochemistry confirmed the lymphocytic type, and viral genome was identified in 3/9 myocarditis cases. The Seaport criteria are a useful tool in the autopsy setting, supporting a standardized approach to the diagnosis of lymphocytic myocarditis. Refinement of these criteria including topographic distribution of inflammation is warranted. The clinical significance of LIUS remains to be assessed in larger series with clinicopathological correlations.
items.journal: Cardiovascular pathology : the official journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Pathology

items.title: PEGylated fucoxanthin liposomes remodel G 0 /G 1 cell cycle homeostasis and suppress gallbladder cancer progression via modulation of NR2F1-mediated signaling networks.
items.abstract: Gallbladder cancer (GBC) is a highly aggressive and refractory biliary malignancy with disordered proliferative homeostasis, rapid malignant progression and scarce effective clinical therapies. Marine fucoxanthin possesses prominent anti-tumor activity, whereas its poor water solubility and low bioavailability limit application, and its core biomolecular mechanism against GBC remains poorly clarified. This study aimed to construct PEGylated fucoxanthin liposomes and elucidate their anti-tumor mechanism targeting biomolecular dynamics and core regulatory targets in GBC. The anti-proliferative, anti-migratory, pro-apoptotic and cell cycle-regulatory effects of fucoxanthin-liposomes were verified using 2D monolayer and physiologically biomimetic 3D GBC spheroid models. Integrative transcriptomic analysis, multi-algorithm machine learning screening, RT-qPCR and immunofluorescence validation were performed to screen core functional targets. Molecular docking and 100 ns molecular dynamics simulations were further conducted to confirm the stable binding characteristics between fucoxanthin and the target protein. Fucoxanthin-liposomes exerted significant dose-dependent inhibitory effects on GBC proliferation and migration, induced mitochondrial structural damage, extensive cell apoptosis, and robust G 0 /G 1 cell cycle arrest. Multi-omics combined with machine learning identified NR2F1 as the pivotal target, whose expression was markedly upregulated after fucoxanthin-liposomes treatment. Fucoxanthin could stably bind NR2F1 through hydrogen bonding and hydrophobic interactions with excellent thermodynamic stability. PEGylated fucoxanthin liposomes restored G 0 /G 1 quiescence-dominated cellular homeostasis and reversed pathological proliferative imbalance in GBC via transcriptional activation of NR2F1. Upregulated NR2F1 remodeled tumor proliferative homeostasis by hierarchically modulating PI3K/AKT/mTOR and JAK2/STAT3 signaling networks, and ultimately restrained GBC clonal proliferation and invasive progression.

items.title: Hepatocellular carcinoma screening in a tertiary hospital. What are we missing?
items.abstract: Screening for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) aims to detect early tumors, with a positive impact on survival. In clinical practice there are several challenges on the application of HCC screening: patients with unknown liver disease, poor patient adherence or problems in the health care system, leading to an underperformance. We aim to evaluate the performance of the HCC screening, the reasons of missed or delayed diagnosis, and prognostic implications in patients with HCC in a tertiary center. Retrospective study including patients with an HCC diagnosis, that have been discussed by a liver tumors board from 2020 to 2023 in a tertiary hospital. HCC screening was defined according to the EASL recommendations. Considering the target population for screening, subgroups were considered and compared: (a) diagnosed through screening; (b) missed screening due to suboptimal patient adherence and/or systemic healthcare inefficiencies; (c) undiagnosed advanced chronic liver disease (uACLD), that would have indication for surveillance if already diagnosed. For patients diagnosed through screening, we considered a margin of 2 months (8 months) as "complete surveillance" and between 8 to 12 months as "incomplete surveillance". To access the survival benefit, we compared the overall survival of the screened population and those do not diagnose through screening. We included 174 patients, 136 had advanced chronic liver disease (ACLD): 70% Child-Pugh (CP) A; 20% CP B; 10% CP C. The most common etiologic factor was excessive alcohol consumption (37%). The proportion of patients diagnosed in screening was 26%. Regarding Barcelona Clinic Liver Cancer (BCLC) stage at diagnosis, 4% BCLC-0, 37% BCLC-A, 10% BCLC-B, 33% BCLC-C and 15% BCLC-D. Patients in subgroup (a) had HCC diagnosed at earlier stages (BCLC-0 and BCLC-A). The subgroup (c) had a higher proportion CP B and C (p = 0.008), vascular invasion (p = 0.01), extrahepatic involvement (p = 0.052) and hepatic dysfunction according to ALBI score (p < 0.001) at time of diagnosis. Overall survival was significantly higher for screened group. In our cohort, only about a quarter of HCC cases were diagnosed through screening, with impact on survival. Among patients with indication for screening, only one third achieved diagnostic yield. Our findings emphasize the need to improve HCC screening strategies and the pivotal role of primary care in the early diagnosis of underlying liver disease.
